summary: Redis reconciliation failed in DB 3. None of the expected credbridge token runtime keys were present for tenant 019d8414-bf83-7641-a3fb-ad93d58715bd or for the four recorded token IDs: the tenant active/revoked keys were absent, every credbridge:token:{id} lookup returned missing with TTL -2, broad scans over credbridge:* and token:blacklist:* returned no matches, and the only key present in DB 3 was an unrelated CHAIN_ERROR_WHITE_LIST set.
contract_findings: DB 3 contained no credbridge:tokens:{tenant_id}:active key for tenant 019d8414-bf83-7641-a3fb-ad93d58715bd.
DB 3 contained no credbridge:tokens:{tenant_id}:revoked key for tenant 019d8414-bf83-7641-a3fb-ad93d58715bd.
DB 3 contained no credbridge:token:{token_id} metadata hash for any recorded token ID, including the current-run active and revoked token IDs.
Broad scans over credbridge:* and token:blacklist:* returned no matches tied to auth, token, session, sandbox, or operation IDs from this run.
The only key present in DB 3 was CHAIN_ERROR_WHITE_LIST, an unrelated persistent set with chain-error strings rather than runtime auth/token state.
PostgreSQL reconciliation shows live issued tokens persisted in credbridge_vault.api_tokens, not scope_tokens; Redis did not carry parallel token runtime state for those IDs.
Source inspection shows auth sessions are PostgreSQL-backed in the live path, so missing session-id keys are supporting evidence rather than the primary contract failure.
